text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool eu-west-1 p99 latency spike detected. p99 > 3s for streaming endpoints for the last 6m. SLOs impacted. Auto-autoscaler reports delayed warmup; queue depth at 85%. Paging on-call.

sam-oncall: acknowledging. joining. Any customer-visible errors?

maria: yes, SLO alert routed from monitor. Affected routes: /v1/stream and /v1/chat on model-id: rdx-llama-13b-quant. Error rate low, but tail latencies and streaming stalls. Seeing significant queueing on dedicated-pool-eu-west-1-hotshot.

kevin-eng: looking at autoscaler logs — handshake/warmup for new GPUs timing out due to nonce mismatch with instance bootstrap. Warmup retries spiking. Might be control-plane rate-limited on provisioning calls.

lucas-sre: metrics:
```
queue_depth_percent = 0.85
p99_latency = 3.2s
p95_latency = 1.1s
streaming_stall_rate = 7%
new_pool_launch_fail_rate = 0.28
```

maya-cust-succ: we have a few customers pinging support about slow streaming on chat. Not yet widespread errors but UX severely degraded for some sessions.

sam-oncall: move to mitigation. Priority: reduce customer-visible p99. Can we shift traffic, fallback to smaller model, or manually scale?

kevin-eng: quick mitigation options:
- temporarily route lowest-priority traffic to hosted fallback (rdx-small)
- lower target batch_size for streaming routes to reduce warmup pressure
- manual add of warm started instances to hotshot pool (fast but intrusive)

ops-bot: Command suggestion: `/infra scale-pool --pool dedicated-eu-west-1-hotshot --count +3 --mode warmstart --reason "incident 1795001111"`

maria: I'll open the routing change for low-priority customers. @kevin-eng can you try manual warmstart? Also enabling prefix KV cache warmup for active sessions.

kevin-eng: running manual scale now. Pasting command and result: 
```
# invoked by kevin-eng
/infra scale-pool --pool dedicated-eu-west-1-hotshot --count 3 --mode warmstart --immediate
Result: request accepted, launch ops id = op-8791, provisioning started
```

lucas-sre: I'm toggling fallback policy to allow up to 20% of traffic to degrade to hosted fallback and restricting heavy batch routes. Doing now.

ops-bot: ACTION: routing rule updated. `policy: fallback-hosted` applied to routes: /v1/stream (priority: low).

maria: KV cache prewarm kicked for ~150 active prefixes. Should reduce cold-KV tail on initial tokens.

kevin-eng: Provisioned instances booted but warmup-hook failed for 2/3 due to a startup race in model-compiler step. Restarting init script with extended timeout.

lucas-sre: while warmstart completes, I'm enabling aggressive dequeue on queue router to prioritize real-time streaming requests over batch rerank jobs.

sam-oncall: any signs of p99 improving?

maria: initial numbers: p95 ~ 0.9s, p99 down to 1.6s from 3.2s after fallbacks + warmstart progress. streaming_stall_rate -> 2.1%. Visible customer complaints dropping. :thumbsup:

kevin-eng: warmstart completed successfully for all new instances. Noted root cause: autoscaler backoff backpressure when control-plane errors > 5/min. There is a bug in the handshake retry limiter that prevents immediate second attempt. Will file PR.

lucas-sre: temporary mitigation held. We extended autoscaler retry window in control-plane config to allow faster retries for hotshot pools. That change is staged and applied.

maya-cust-succ: flagged affected tenants and sent interim status update: "We're experiencing elevated streaming latency in EU region. Primary mitigation in progress; some sessions may fall back to a hosted path for reduced quality while we stabilize."

sam-oncall: good. Next: schedule follow-up postmortem and customer RCA. Assign owners: kevin -> root cause + fix; lucas -> autoscaler config and runbook update; maria -> customer comms and telemetry validation; sam -> postmortem writeup and SLA impact calc.

kevin-eng: started GH issue: "autoscaler: handshake retry limiter causes warmup delay under provisioning errors". PR reference: TBD.

lucas-sre: updating on-call runbook with a new play to "force-warmstart" and a checklist for toggling fallback-hosted policy and KV prewarm steps.

maria: final metrics snapshot before close: p95 0.85s, p99 0.98s, streaming_stall_rate 0.9%, queue_depth 22%. Customer-visible errors resolved.

sam-oncall: closing live incident channel. Leaving thread open for owners to post RCA and timeline. If anything regresses, re-ping @pagerduty. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: incident 1795001111 marked resolved by sam-oncall. Duration: ~55m. SLA impact: partial degraded performance; no data loss. Postmortem scheduled for 2025-08-12 15:00 UTC.

kevin-eng: note for postmortem: consider proactive warmstart sequencing for hotshot pools on forecasted traffic spikes and introduce a circuit-breaker to fall back to hosted earlier to avoid customer p99 breaches.

lucas-sre: adding runbook link: https://redwood.example.internal/runbooks/dedicated-warmup-warmstart (please review before postmortem)

maria: thanks all. I'll consolidate customer messages and update support tickets with status and mitigation details.

sam-oncall: night crew, please watch EU hotshot pool during next 24h. I'll add extra monitor and an alert for autoscaler-provision-fail-rate > 0.1/min.

maya-cust-succ: cc @product for potential UX work to surfacing degraded-mode to customers gracefully.

kevin-eng: PR opened and link posted in PM thread. Will follow up on rollback if any warmstart regressions seen.

sam-oncall: end of thread—postmortem to include timeline, impact, RCA, corrective actions, and owners.

incident-bot: INCIDENT THREAD CLOSED.
